title: [Homepage] Featured + DAC cards match catalogue card style
description:
GOAL (what the shopper sees)
On the homepage Featured section and DAC section, each product card adopts the catalogue ProductCard style - adjusted for homepage use - so the cream product-image area is expanded edge-to-edge to the card's side and top edges instead of sitting in a thick inset frame. Same calm one-unit composition as the catalogue card (quiet brand line, readable title, understated price, small add control), reusing the sang-logium-6cm tokens (.type-product-brand / .type-product-title / .type-product-price / .btn-product-add). Applies only to the Featured section and the DAC section - no other homepage rail.

Current status: FeaturedCard (app/components/features/homepage/featured/Featured.tsx) and DacCard (app/components/features/homepage/dacs/DacCard.tsx) both use card-product-dark (24px padding, never overridden) and a figure with its own inner p-5 / p-6 + rounded-lg, so the cream bg-surface-productImage area is inset with a thick top/side frame. Title/price/brand/add-button use ad-hoc text-xs / text-small / text-tiny + type-price + default .btn-cart, not the 6cm product tokens. Catalogue ProductCard already went edge-to-edge via !p-0 overflow-hidden + flush figure in sang-logium-dbu; this issue replicates that on the two homepage sections.

title: [Product Cards] Shared design tokens in tailwind.config
description:
GOAL (what the shopper sees)
Every product card - catalogue grid, search, wishlist, and the homepage rails
(Best Sellers, DACs, IEMs, Accessories) - draws its brand line, title, price and
add button from ONE shared, correctly-scaled set of design-system tokens, so the
same card looks the same everywhere and reads at high-end-audio proportions
(quiet brand line, ~13-14px title, ~14-15px price, small secondary add button)
instead of each surface inventing its own oversized sizing.

SCOPE
Define the tokens in tailwind.config.ts and adopt them in the canonical
ProductCard + the two grid skeletons. Migrating the homepage card variants
(Featured, DacCard, AccessoryCard, IemCard, RelatedProducts) onto the same
tokens is the immediate follow-up, NOT this issue. Do not change the generic
tokens `type-body`, `type-price`, `.btn-cart`, `.card-product-dark` - they stay
for checkout / basket / PDP.

CURRENT STATUS
The card pulls from generic tokens - `type-body` (16px) for the title,
`type-price` (clamp 16->22px, 0.1em letter-spacing) for the price, `.btn-cart`
(14px / weight 700 / 8px padding) for the button - all oversized for a grid
card. Homepage variants each override with ad-hoc `text-xs` / `text-small` /
`text-body` + per-breakpoint tweaks. No product-card-specific token exists
(`.type-card-title` is defined at 16px/600 but unused by ProductCard).

TOKENS TO ADD (component classes in `uiComponentsPlugin` via `addComponents`,
matching the existing `.type-*` / `.btn-*` pattern; final values dialled in on
the live check, within these high-end-audio ranges):
- `.type-product-brand`  ~10-11px, uppercase, letter-spacing ~0.08em,
                         weight 400-500, muted (caption colour)
- `.type-product-title`  ~13-14px, weight 500, line-height ~1.4, normal
                         tracking, body colour
- `.type-product-price`  ~14-15px, weight 600, tabular-nums, normal
                         letter-spacing, price-tag colour
- `.btn-product-add`     compact add-to-cart: ~12-13px, weight 600, padding
                         ~7px 10px, gap ~6px, icon ~14px, accent-500 fill,
                         radius sm, and the SAME hover / focus-visible /
                         active / disabled block as `.btn-cart`

------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACCEPTANCE TESTS  (human, live, localhost:3000 - implementing agent does NOT
verify)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  T1. On /products, /search, /account/wishlist: card title computes to <=14px;
      price ~14-15px with even (non-0.1em) letter-spacing; add-button text
      <=13px.
  T2. Brand line is visibly smaller and quieter than the title.
  T3. The add button keeps the gold fill and the hover / focus-visible /
      disabled behaviour of the old `.btn-cart`, just smaller.
  T4. Skeleton placeholder bars line up with the new text sizes - no shift
      when cards load (375 / 768 / 1280 / 1600).
  T5. Checkout, basket, the PDP buy-box and the homepage rails are visually
      unchanged (generic tokens untouched).
  T6. No console errors; no horizontal scroll.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEPS
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. tailwind.config.ts -> add `.type-product-brand`, `.type-product-title`,
   `.type-product-price`, `.btn-product-add` to `uiComponentsPlugin`. Use
   `theme(...)` refs for colour / spacing; copy `.btn-cart`'s full
   hover/focus/active/disabled block into `.btn-product-add`.
2. Resolve `.type-card-title`: grep its usages - if unused, delete it; if used,
   leave it and note why it differs. Do not ship two title tokens for the card.
3. ProductCard.tsx -> brand `type-caption` -> `type-product-brand`; title
   `type-body` -> `type-product-title` (keep `line-clamp-2`); price
   `<Price className="type-product-price tabular-nums" />`.
4. BasketControls.tsx -> add optional `addClassName?: string`; render the add
   button as `className={addClassName || "btn-cart"}` (pick ONE base class,
   never both). ProductCard passes `addClassName="btn-product-add"`.
5. ProductGridSkeleton.tsx + ProductChunkSkeleton.tsx -> resize the
   brand / title / price placeholder bars to the new token sizes.
6. Hand to the human for T1-T6.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
FOOTPRINT: tailwind.config.ts (4 new component classes), ProductCard.tsx,
ProductGridSkeleton.tsx, ProductChunkSkeleton.tsx, BasketControls.tsx (one
optional prop). No deps, no tooling, no git.

DEPENDENCY: blocks sang-logium-dbu (card layout / label / 8+/10 polish builds
on these tokens).
acceptance_criteria: Human live check on :3000: card title <=14px, price ~14-15px non-0.1em tracking, add-button text <=13px with the old gold fill + hover/focus/disabled; brand quieter than title; skeleton matches; checkout/basket/PDP/homepage rails visually unchanged; no console errors. See T1-T6.

title: [Filters] Product grid sizing fits device space with sidebar
description:
GOAL (what the shopper sees)
On every product grid, each card reads as one calm unit: a crisp full-bleed
product image that does the selling, a quiet brand line, a readable 2-line
title, an understated price, and a small unobtrusive add control. Nothing
shouts or crowds; a row of 3-5 cards looks like a single harmonious block, the
way a high-end audio retailer's listing does (Focal, Bang & Olufsen, Bowers &
Wilkins, Sennheiser, Bloom Audio, Audio46). Target: 8+/10 on card layout,
composition and element sizing, live-checked by a human.

DEPENDS ON: sang-logium-6cm (product-card design tokens). 6cm sets the type
scale - brand / title / price / add-button sizes. THIS issue is the card's
layout, composition, label and final polish on top of those tokens. Do not
start until 6cm's tokens are in.

SCOPE
Card layout & composition only: ProductCard.tsx + the two skeletons (+ the
`label` prop already on BasketControls). NOT the type scale (6cm), NOT the grid
column mechanism (done, below), NOT shared tokens `type-body` / `type-price` /
`.btn-cart` / `.card-product-dark` (used by checkout / basket / PDP), NOT the
filter/sort surface (fi0).

DONE 2026-08-30 (regression-check only)
Grid columns: 2 (phone) -> 3 (tablet) -> 3-4 (sidebar desktop) -> 4-5 (search /
wide) via `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-products` + gridTemplateColumns `products`
= repeat(auto-fill, minmax(13.5-15rem, 1fr)); xs:/sm: cascade bug fixed;
aspect-[4/3], min-w-0, max-w-catalogue, skeleton unification all in. ~8/10 -
leave it.

REMAINING PROBLEM (after 6cm lands the type scale)
- Card padding 24px (`card-product-dark`, never overridden) + inner 12px -> the
  image sits in a thick frame, text is inset 36px.
- Title has a fixed `h-10` (reserves 2 lines even for 1-line names) and
  `break-words` -> mid-word truncation ("Dragon.Tail").
- Add button label "Add to Cart" is long; on the narrowest card it crowds the
  price on the same row.
- Brand sits over the image - fine, but confirm it reads as secondary once
  `.type-product-brand` is applied.

TARGET
- Card: add `!p-0 overflow-hidden` to the `card-product-dark` element; product
  image goes edge-to-edge to the card's side edges; text block padding ~12px
  (`p-3`); keep the 1px hairline border.
- Image: keep aspect-[4/3] (1:1 acceptable); product centred with internal
  breathing room.
- Title: `line-clamp-2` with a 2-line min-height (~2.5em), NO `break-words`;
  long names clip cleanly at a word boundary.
- Add control: label "Add" (icon + "Add"); sits inline to the right of the
  price, OR full-width under the price if the card is < ~260px wide.
- Row gap: keep 24px (20px acceptable).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACCEPTANCE TESTS  (human, live, localhost:3000 - resize the real window;
implementing agent does NOT verify)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Surfaces: /products/headphones, /products, /search?q=hd, /account/wishlist.
Also open a product with a very long name and one priced $1,199.
  T1. A row of 4-5 cards reads as one calm block; no single element dominates;
      the 6cm type sizes (title <=14px, price ~14-15px, button <=13px) still
      hold here.
  T2. Title: max 2 lines, wraps at word boundaries (no mid-word "Dragon.Tail"),
      long names clip cleanly; 1-line names don't leave a dead gap.
  T3. Product image is flush to the card's side edges - no thick inner frame;
      text is inset ~12px.
  T4. On the narrowest card (search at >=1536px, ~275px) the price and the add
      control share one line with no overlap/wrap, OR the button is full-width
      below the price.
  T5. Brand line reads as clearly secondary to the title.
  T6. Skeleton matches the loaded card (padding, image box, text positions) -
      no shift when cards load (375 / 768 / 1280 / 1600).
  T7. Cards equal height per row; grid column counts unchanged from the current
      build; no console errors; no horizontal scroll.
  Overall: card layout + composition read 8+/10 vs a high-end audio retailer -
  the human's call.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEPS  (after sang-logium-6cm is merged)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. ProductCard `<article>`: add `!p-0 overflow-hidden`. Give the text wrapper
   `p-3`; keep the price row `px-3 pb-3` (or merge into one `p-3` block).
2. Title: drop `h-10` and `break-words`; use `line-clamp-2 min-h-[2.5em]`.
3. ProductCard: pass `label="Add"` to BasketControls; decide inline vs
   full-width from T4 (stack the price/button column if the narrowest card
   crowds).
4. Mirror steps 1-2 in ProductGridSkeleton + ProductChunkSkeleton (card
   padding, image box flush, placeholder positions).
5. Run the CLAUDE.md height-sizing diff review on the padding / min-height
   changes, then hand to the human for the T1-T7 live check.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
FOOTPRINT: ProductCard.tsx, ProductGridSkeleton.tsx, ProductChunkSkeleton.tsx
(BasketControls only via the existing `label` prop). No token edits, no deps,
no tooling, no git.
acceptance_criteria: PREREQ: sang-logium-6cm tokens merged. Human live check on :3000, all 4 grid surfaces + a long-name / $1,199 product: card reads as one calm unit; image flush to card edges; title 2-line word-wrapped no dead gap; add control not crowding the narrowest card (inline or full-width); brand secondary; 6cm sizes still hold; skeleton matches; columns unchanged; equal heights; no console errors. 8+/10 card layout vs a high-end audio retailer. See T1-T7.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (2026-08-30, rev 4 - card layout/composition on top of the 6cm
tokens; supersedes earlier notes)

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Redoing 6cm's work or editing a shared token. The type scale (brand /
    title / price / add-button sizes) belongs to sang-logium-6cm; the generic
    tokens `type-body` / `type-price` / `.btn-cart` / `.card-product-dark`
    belong to checkout / basket / PDP. MITIGATE: this issue only changes card
    padding, image bleed, title height, the label text, and inline-vs-stacked;
    it references tokens, never defines or edits them.
A2. h-full / height-ownership regression (CLAUDE.md mandatory review gate +
    docs/vertical-space-lg-touch.md). `!p-0`, moved padding, and `h-10` ->
    min-height on the title change the card box height. MITIGATE: step 5 runs
    the height-sizing diff review; the title keeps an explicit 2-line
    min-height; the image box keeps its explicit aspect; T7 checks equal
    heights.
A3. Scope creep into the grid or the fi0 filter/sort surface. MITIGATE: no
    edits to gridLayout.ts, the flex row, page wrappers, or any filter/sort
    file; grid column counts are a regression check only (T7).
A4. Price + add control collide on the narrowest card (~250-275px). MITIGATE:
    T4 targets exactly that card; the documented fallback is a full-width
    button below the price (step 3).
A5. Skeleton drift -> CLS. MITIGATE: step 4 mirrors every card change; T6
    eyeballs it at 4 widths.
A6. Long words overflow once `break-words` is removed. MITIGATE: `line-clamp-2`
    + `overflow-hidden` clips cleanly at 2 lines regardless of word length; T2
    checks a long-name product on the narrowest card.
A7. Starting before 6cm merges -> rework when token names/sizes land. MITIGATE:
    hard dependency; do not start step 1 until 6cm is in.
A8. False "8+/10" claim. MITIGATE: the agent reports measured px + the
    inline/stacked decision per surface; the verdict is the human's live check.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS (lean path - standing rule) ==
Source className edits only, then hand to the human's dev server on
localhost:3000.
B1. No next build.               B6. No npm install / new dependency.
B2. No tsc / ts-check.           B7. No git (branch / commit / push).
B3. No project lint / prettier.  B8. No subagents; read files inline.
B4. No test runs, no new tests.  B9. No new docs / long analysis.
B5. No agent-run dev server, no browser automation for verification -
    the human resizes the window.
B10. Minimal diff - no reformatting untouched code.
If a hard NO genuinely blocks the task, stop and say so in one plain line.

title: [Filters] Shared URL param contract for filter + sort state
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: This issue defines the single shared vocabulary for filter/sort URL state - every param key, its value type, its default, its parse and serialize rules, the history mode (replace vs push), and the clean-URL rule (a param sitting at its default never appears in the URL) - as nuqs parsers plus a loader, exported for F2-F6 to import. It also defines the shared "pending" affordance shown while a URL transition is in flight. It is headless: no visible UI of its own. It does not fetch data and does not know about, import, query, or react to the product grid, product data, result counts, or streaming.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS - human live check on the dev server at localhost:3000. F1 has no UI, so these are checked by hand-typing catalogue URLs and watching the address bar, verified against the first consuming control (F2) once it exists:

- When I load a catalogue URL with a filter/sort param set to its default value, then once the page settles the address bar shows that param removed (defaults never persist in the URL).
- When I load a catalogue URL with a filter/sort param holding a junk value, then the page still renders (no crash, no error overlay) and the param is treated as unset.
- When I change one filter/sort control and then press the browser Back button, then the address bar returns to the exact previous URL, and Forward re-applies it.
- When I change a control, then the page does not do a full white reload - the change is a soft URL update.
- When any control writes the URL, then unrelated query params already present (e.g. ?q= from search, ?page= from pagination) are preserved untouched.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Any visible control (V1/V2 and F2-F6).
- Whether the product grid reacts to the params (page-composition concern, not this contract).
- Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.

RISK ASSESSMENT

Outcome risks (wrong result / mix-up / hallucination / false positive)
- Reviving the deleted lib/catalogue/filterParams.ts / sortParams.ts / searchParams.ts verbatim. They encoded the OLD removed system's shape (compound ?f=brand:x syntax, a server-side sort allowlist, shallow:false + router.replace to force an RSC refetch). Mitigation: design the contract fresh for the V1/F-layer's client-only needs; treat the deleted files as reference for nuqs mechanics only, not for the schema or the routing model.
- Param-key collisions. /products and /products/[...slug] already parse ?page= by hand; /search owns ?q=. Mitigation: enumerate every param already read on those three routes first; choose filter keys that never clash; the contract must round-trip unrelated params untouched.
- Wrong history/shallow choice. The old system used shallow:false to trigger a server round-trip; this layer is client-only display sync and almost certainly wants shallow:true (no refetch) with an explicit replace-vs-push decision per param. Mitigation: state the choice and its consequence in the contract; the Product Grid observes URL changes independently via the existing lib/catalogue/urlChangeEvents.ts (locationchange) - filters never call the grid.
- Clean-URL rule wrong: defaults serialized into the URL. This makes URLs ugly and trips lib/catalogue/seo.ts isFacetedQuery (canonical/noindex logic keys off query presence). Mitigation: default value => param absent; sanity-check against isFacetedQuery.
- Price unit ambiguity. Product price_data.unit_amount is cents; the UI works in dollars (lib/catalogue/priceBounds.ts, centsToDisplay). Mitigation: the contract fixes the URL unit explicitly (dollars, integer) and F3 converts for display; write it down.
- "Does changing a filter reset ?page=?" left undecided, so F2-F6 each guess. Mitigation: decide it here (recommended: a filter/sort write resets page to 1) and expose it as one helper the controls call.
- nuqs API drift. Installed is nuqs ^2.8.3. Mitigation: confirm the exact installed version and the API surface used (parseAsString/parseAsInteger/parseAsArrayOf, useQueryState(s), createLoader/createSerializer) before writing.

Execution risks (unnecessary work / time cost)
- Headless issue => strongest pull to "just run tsc / a build to check it compiles". Mitigation: none of tsc / ts-check / build / lint / tests / npm install - inspection only.
- No dev server: F1 has no UI; verification piggybacks on F2. Mitigation: do not start a server or browser automation.
- Writing a separate contract design doc. Mitigation: the contract lives in code + this issue body; no new docs.
- Over-scoping into GROQ filter-builders, Sanity loaders, or grid wiring. Mitigation: headless parsers + a loader/serializer only; zero data access; no commit/push unless asked.

Expected footprint: one small module under lib/catalogue/ (e.g. filterSortParams.ts) exporting the parsers, a loader, a serializer and the page-reset helper. No component, dependency or config changes.

SEQUENCE: Can start immediately (independent of V1). Blocks F2-F6.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started. nuqs is already a project dependency (^2.8.3); no filter/sort param contract exists on main.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-08-30)

== A. OUTCOME RISKS (wrong result, mix-up, hallucination, quality drop) ==

A1. Contract leaks past headless.
    F1 must be pure vocabulary - parsers, loader, a pending affordance. Risk: it starts importing
    the grid, product data, counts, or streaming, or renders a visible control.
    MITIGATE: no JSX control of its own; no import of grid/data/count/streaming modules. If it
    can't be built without them, the boundary is wrong - stop and flag.

A2. Clean-URL rule implemented halfway.
    "A param at its default never appears in the URL" is easy to get wrong for arrays, ranges,
    and the sort default.
    MITIGATE: every parser gets an explicit default + clearOnDefault; write the rule once in the
    loader, not per-consumer.

A3. History mode / param-preservation wrong.
    Wrong replace-vs-push, or clobbering unrelated params (?q= from search) on write.
    MITIGATE: decide replace vs push per the issue and note it inline; always MERGE, never
    replace, the query object on write.

A4. Over-designing the contract.
    Inventing param keys, value shapes, or a generic facet framework F2-F6 don't need yet.
    MITIGATE: define exactly the keys F2-F6 name (sort, price min/max, in-stock, brand + one more
    facet group) - nothing speculative.

A5. nuqs SSR / adapter drift.
    Missing NuqsAdapter in the tree, or a loader that doesn't match the parsers -> first-load /
    deep-link mismatch.
    MITIGATE: one source of truth - a single parsers object imported by both the loader and the
    consumers.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS (agent adds fat instead of the lean path) ==

Lean path = write the parser/loader module (+ the pending affordance), hand off. Human checks on :3000.

B1. No build / tsc / lint / test runs.
B2. No agent-run dev server or browser automation.
B3. nuqs is already a dependency - no npm install, no alternative lib.
B4. No new architecture docs - the contract is short comments in the module.
B5. No scaffolding for F2-F6 - just export what they import.
B6. No subagents - this is one small module.
B7. Ignore git - no commits, no branch work.

Expected footprint: 1-2 new files (e.g. lib/catalogue/filterParams.ts + a small pending-state
helper), possibly one NuqsAdapter mount if not already present.

F1 implemented (2026-08-30). New files only, no component/dep/config changes:
- lib/catalogue/filterSortParams.ts — parser map (sort/minPrice/maxPrice/inStock/brand/category), loadFilterSort loader, serializeFilterSort serializer, SORT_OPTIONS allowlist, FILTER_SORT_URL_OPTIONS, contract docs in header. Keys checked against existing page/q/drawer — no clash.
- app/hooks/nuqs/useFilterSort.tsx — useFilterParam (shared options + page-reset baked in), usePageReset, useClearAllFilters, FilterSortPendingProvider + useFilterSortPending (nuqs 2.8 has no isLoading, so pending = React useTransition wired through context).
Decisions: URL price unit = whole dollars; discrete controls history:push, price history:replace (F3); all shallow:true; filter/sort write resets ?page= to 1; defaults never serialized (clearOnDefault). NuqsAdapter already mounted in app/(store)/layout.tsx. No tsc/build/lint/test run per Part B.
close_reason: F1 implemented 2026-08-30: lib/catalogue/filterSortParams.ts (parser map, loadFilterSort, serializeFilterSort, SORT_OPTIONS, FILTER_SORT_URL_OPTIONS) + app/hooks/nuqs/useFilterSort.tsx (useFilterParam, usePageReset, useClearAllFilters, FilterSortPendingProvider). Headless contract only; no visible control wired (that is F2-F6). Verified no build/tsc/lint per Part B.

title: [Filters] Desktop filter panel + sort bar visual shell
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: This issue delivers only the static desktop appearance of the filters/sorting surface, built from the project design system (tailwind.config.ts tokens + type-* utilities), matching the archived components at commit f4f3026a^ (app/components/features/filters/: FilterSidebar, PriceRangeSlider, SortDropdown, and the shared section-header / slider primitives they export). It does not read or write the URL, does not use query params, does not fetch data, and does not filter, sort, count, or otherwise touch the product grid or streaming. All options, counts and price bounds are hardcoded placeholders. Any state is local and cosmetic only (expand/collapse a group, ticked look).

ACCEPTANCE TESTS - human live check on the dev server at localhost:3000, desktop-width window, on a category page (e.g. /products/headphones) and on /products:

Layout
- When I open the page at desktop width, then I see a filter panel on the left and the product grid to its right.
- When I look at the filter panel, then it reads as one finished card (soft border, slightly raised background, same visual language as other cards on the site), not a plain box bolted on.

Panel contents
- When I look at the panel top, then I see a "Filters" heading.
- When I scan down the panel, then I see, in this order: a price range control, an "In stock only" checkbox, a "Brand" group, and at least one more facet group.
- When I look at the price control, then I see a two-handle slider with min and max value labels, and the track / handle / gold active-fill match the site's design system.
- When I look at the "Brand" group, then I see a group label and a list of options, each with a checkbox and a small count beside it.
- When a brand option has a count of zero, then it appears dimmed / disabled.
- When I check fonts, colours and spacing against the rest of the site, then nothing looks like a raw browser default (no blue underlined links, no system font, no misaligned native checkboxes).

Sort + count bar
- When I look above the product grid, then I see a "Sort by" control and a line showing a result count.
- When I open the sort control, then I see a list of options (Featured, Price low-to-high, Price high-to-low, Newest, Name A-Z).

Cosmetic interactions (look only)
- When I click a group header (e.g. "Brand"), then that group collapses and hides its options; clicking again expands it.
- When I click a checkbox, then it shows a ticked state.
- When I pick a different sort option, then the control's label updates to show my choice.

Nothing actually works (the hard guarantee)
- When I tick/untick any checkbox, drag the price handles, collapse a group, or change the sort option, then the product grid stays identical (same products, same order, same count).
- When I do any of the above, then the page URL stays exactly the same (no query params appear).
- When I reload the page, then every checkbox and collapsed group returns to its default look (nothing was remembered).

OUT OF SCOPE
- Narrow / mobile / tablet widths and the lg-touch breakpoint (handled in V2).
- Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour (later layer).
- Any URL, data, or product-grid behaviour (functional layer F1-F6).

RISK ASSESSMENT

Outcome risks (wrong result / mix-up / hallucination / false positive)
- Wrong source: f4f3026a is the DELETION commit; the components live at its parent f4f3026a^. Mitigation: read via `git show f4f3026a^:app/components/features/filters/<file>`.
- Porting the wired archive by mistake. Two archived copies exist: the static one at app/components/features/filters/ (f4f3026a^) and a fully URL-wired one at product-building-center/filters_archived/ (with useFilterNuqs / useRangeSlider / useDrawerState). Mitigation: copy only from the static path; never open filters_archived/; strip any import of a hook, store, useSearchParams, nuqs or router; options/counts/bounds stay hardcoded inline.
- "Finishing" the feature: adding real state, URL or data because it feels unfinished. Mitigation: the "Nothing actually works" acceptance tests are the gate - any wiring shipped fails the issue.
- Design-token drift. The archived components mix token names from different eras (text-text-accent vs text-accent-500, bg-surface-elevated, type-overline, bg-brand-100). Some resolve on current main, some may not. Mitigation: carry the archived classes over, then grep tailwind.config.ts and app/globals.css to confirm each class exists; for the card shell reuse an existing sibling card's exact border/bg/shadow classes; no raw hex, no default palette, no invented class names.
- Real data creeping in: fetching brands or counts from Sanity to look realistic. Mitigation: hardcoded arrays only; no GROQ; no imports from sanity-cms/.
- Wrong stock control: porting the archived StockMinimumSlider. Mitigation: "In stock only" is a plain checkbox using the existing app/components/ui/Checkbox.tsx - the archived slider is not used.

The sidebar adds sticky / self-start / height classes next to ChunkedProductGrid, and CLAUDE.md has a mandatory review gate for any h-full / min-h- / max-h- / aspect- change under app/components/**. title: [Product Images] Harden pipeline + replace invalid inventory images
description:
﻿Some inventory images across the product catalogue are currently forged/invalid and must be replaced in bulk. Additionally, the product image upload pipeline must be hardened so that uploaded images never include backgrounds and never exceed acceptable size limits.

The project already has a dedicated external data folder (with dashes in its name, located outside the repo root) that contains RemBG background-removal tooling and image size-management utilities. The replacement and upload pipeline should be wired to run product images through that folder's existing processing steps.

Please begin by:

- Auditing the current product image inventory and pipeline to identify all forged/invalid images and their source/Sanity mappings.
- Inspecting the external Sanglogium data folder to document the existing RemBG and image-size-management capabilities.
- Proposing a replacement pipeline that removes backgrounds, enforces size limits, validates output, and re-uploads only clean images.
- Implementing the minimal safe first slice to prevent new invalid images from entering the pipeline.

## Proposed remaining pipeline steps

### Phase 0 — Audit current inventory

1. Run a Sanity-wide audit of every `product` document, collecting for each main image and gallery image:
   - `_id`, `name`, `slug`, `catalogueLocationKeys`
   - `image.asset._ref`, `originalFilename`, `url`, `metadata.dimensions`, `sha1hash`
   - duplicate-asset counts across products
2. Flag as invalid any image that is:
   - missing or tiny (`< 200px`)
   - a placeholder/wrong filename
   - a duplicate shared by more than 2 products
   - a main product image with a non-transparent / non-removed background
   - over size limits (`> 1 MB` main, `> 1.2 MB` gallery, or `> 1600px` max dimension)
3. Output `image-audit-report.json` with severity groups and source-to-Sanity mappings.

### Phase 1 — Harden the ingestion pipeline (minimal safe first slice)

1. Add a post-processing validation step to `sang-logium-data/src/image-pipeline.ts` that runs **after** `rembg_remove.py` / `compress_gallery.py` and **before** `assets.upload`:
   - Main image: PNG must have alpha; edges must be > 70% transparent; dimensions and file size must be under `1600px` / `1 MB`.
   - Gallery image: JPEG must be under `1600px` / `1.2 MB`; quality no lower than `75`.
   - Failures are rejected and logged; no bad asset enters Sanity.
2. Wire `sang-logium` (main repo) manual image paths to the external pipeline:
   - Add a small adapter script in `sang-logium` that calls `sang-logium-data/scripts/rembg_remove.py` and `compress_gallery.py` for any image before it is uploaded/patched.
   - Update `scripts/patch-botched-product-images.mjs` to route each image through the adapter and apply the same validation.

title: [Filters] Active-filter chips + Clear all <-> URL
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: This control's only responsibility: (a) on user interaction, write the correct value to the URL via nuqs; (b) on URL change - including first load, deep link, and browser back/forward - render its own display to match the URL. It does not know about, import, query, or react to the product grid, product data, result counts, or streaming. It reads the same shared param contract from F1 that F2-F5 write.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS - human live check on the dev server at localhost:3000, watching the address bar, starting from a URL that already has several filter + sort params set, on /products/headphones and /products:

Happy path
- When I load a URL with brand, price and sort params set, then I see one chip per active value, with price shown as a single range chip.
- When I click the X on a brand chip, then that value leaves the brand param in the address bar and the chip disappears; other chips and params stay.
- When I click "Clear all", then every filter and sort param is removed from the address bar in a single step, and all chips disappear.
- When there are no active filters, then the chip row and "Clear all" are absent (or "Clear all" is disabled).
- When I remove a chip, then the page does not do a full white reload.

Edge path
- When I click "Clear all" while a search query param is also in the URL, then that query param stays and only the filter/sort params are removed.
- When I press Back right after "Clear all", then all the previous filters and their chips come back in lockstep with the address bar.
- When a param in the URL holds a value with no matching label, then its chip shows the raw value cleanly or is omitted - never a broken or blank chip.
- When price is set to only one bound, then the range chip reads sensibly (e.g. "From $X" or "Up to $Y").

OUT OF SCOPE
- Whether the product grid actually updates when a chip is removed.
- Visual styling (V1), mobile (V2), keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.

RISK ASSESSMENT

Outcome risks (wrong result / mix-up / hallucination / false positive)
- Chips deriving state from a local mirror that drifts from the URL. Mitigation: chips are a pure render of F1's parsed URL state; the only write path is F1's setters.
- "Clear all" nuking unrelated params - ?q= (search), ?page= (pagination). Mitigation: clear only the explicit F1 filter/sort key list; the "?q= survives Clear all" test is the gate.
- "Clear all" producing one history entry per param, so Back needs many presses to undo. Mitigation: a single batched setter call (useQueryStates / F1 serializer) => one history entry.
- Inventing display labels for values. The human-readable labels come from the same option lists F5 receives as props. Mitigation: F6 takes a label-resolver prop; raw-value fallback; never a blank chip.
- Price rendered as two separate chips, or a one-sided range reading wrong. Mitigation: explicit range-chip rule ("$X-$Y", "From $X", "Up to $Y") - one chip for the pair.
- Building F6 before F2-F5 exist and guessing their param keys. Mitigation: F6 is sequenced last; every key and parser is imported from F1.
- Reacting to the grid / result count (e.g. "Clear all" only when results are empty). Mitigation: SRP - URL in, URL out.

Execution risks (unnecessary work / time cost)
- tsc / ts-check / build / lint / tests / npm install. Mitigation: none - forbidden; inspection only.
- Agent-run dev server or browser automation. Mitigation: the human does the :3000 address-bar check.
- A chip / tag UI library. Mitigation: small static markup styled with V1's tokens; zero new deps.
- Also wiring the grid to prove removal re-queries. Mitigation: out of scope; ends at the URL.
- No new docs; no commit/push unless asked.

Expected footprint: one client component that reads all F1 params, maps them to chips with a label resolver, and calls per-key clear + a batched clear-all from F1. No dependency or config changes.

SEQUENCE: After F1, V1, and F2-F5.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started.

description:

* solution cannot interfere with solution of streaming ux: products appearing faster in smaller chunks, instead of taking longer and appearing all at once as one big wall

Current status: Attempt G on working tree - the professional, ship-able solution. A small "use client" RevealImage wrapper (the standard next/image reveal, same as Vercel's commerce template): onLoad -> setState -> class, state also seeded from a ref callback checking img.complete so priority/cached images reveal at once. F.1 failed here because it used opacity:0 gated on client state, so images stayed invisible until their leaf hydrated and then flipped in a burst = one wall, later.
